transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
I’m exhausted all the time, like I’m worn out before the day even starts, and I can’t seem to get my energy back. It just feels like no matter how much I try to rest, I'm completely drained.
How long have you been feeling this exhausted, and has this happened before in separate periods or is this the first time?

It started about seven or eight months ago when I transitioned into my full-time lab job, and it has pretty much been my default state every single day since. It hasn't really happened in separate periods—it's just been this constant, heavy exhaustion that I haven't been able to shake.

Along with the exhaustion, have you also been feeling persistently depressed or unable to enjoy things most days, and has it ever gotten so severe that you struggled to do basic daily tasks like getting out of bed, washing, or eating?

I don't really feel persistently depressed, and I haven't struggled with getting out of bed or basic hygiene. But I am often too exhausted to cook real meals, so I just resort to instant noodles, and I've completely stopped doing hobbies I used to enjoy like painting and hiking because I'm just so drained.

Besides feeling physically exhausted, do you also find that even small mental tasks—like reading, concentrating, or problem-solving—quickly wear you out or make it hard to think clearly? Or is it mainly your body that feels drained?

It's mainly my body that feels incredibly heavy and physically drained. My mind doesn't really feel slow or foggy—it's actually the opposite, constantly racing with worries and replaying mistakes, which makes it hard to focus on other things rather than just lacking mental energy.

Do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different parts of life on most days, and is it hard to control the worrying even when you try to stop? Have you also had symptoms like feeling keyed up, tense, irritable, restless, or trouble sleeping along with it?

Yes, my mind constantly spirals with uncontrollable worries about everything from lab calibration to my parents' health in El Salvador, and I just can't shut it off. Physically, I feel wound up like I've had way too much coffee—constantly pacing and jumping at notifications—while my shoulders, neck, and jaw are always tight and aching from tension.

How has your sleep been during this time—do you have trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or wake up feeling unrefreshed because your worries keep going? About how many nights a week does that happen?

I'm not really sure if I have specific trouble falling or staying asleep, but I constantly wake up feeling completely unrefreshed and exhausted. It's like I've pulled an all-nighter in the lab, and it happens almost every single day.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes excessive, difficult-to-control worry across multiple life domains on most days for 7–8 months, accompanied by restlessness/keyed-up feeling, muscle tension, impaired concentration due to worry, and chronically unrefreshing sleep/fatigue. Depressive syndrome is not supported because the patient denies persistent depressed mood and severe loss of basic functioning, and the presentation is better explained by generalized anxiety than by a primary fatigue disorder.
